verdicts.reason: Both remove the coffee bag from the hero photo, leaving a blank blurred brown rectangle, and shrink the bag to a postage-stamp icon by the logo. A also leaves the CTA tiny and buried at the bottom, with an unreadable label and a minuscule logo, below a dead top band. B's CTA is a little larger and the logo more legible, but the CTA sits orphaned above the headline (odd reading order) and the oversized SAVE 15% badge competes with the headline.

Both have the same faults: a small CTA stranded at the top, a product-less blurred image block, a bag shrunk to an icon, and an oversized badge. A at least keeps headline and body together at the top, under the CTA. B puts the empty image between the CTA and the headline, so the eye meets a meaningless brown box before any message.

A has a weak hierarchy: the CTA is isolated at the top, the image is empty and the bag is reduced to an icon. Still, the text is large and readable. B is the original shrunk and letterboxed into the middle of the tall canvas, with roughly two thirds dead space and body copy and CTA too small to read: unusable.

A has a readable headline and body, but the bag is gone from the photo, and the CTA and logo are tiny and crammed into the bottom-left corner, under an oversized badge. B is the same letterboxed shrink of the original, with large empty bands and illegible microtext.
